title: Vintage Gibson LG Series Value Guide: Prices By Year
description: Compare vintage Gibson LG-0, LG-1, LG-2 and LG-3 values by model and era, with original parts, bracing, repair details and photos from my archive.
h1: Vintage Gibson LG Series Value Guide
alt: Sunburst LG-2 with a rectangular bridge and a large mottled pickguard

faqs.q: How Much Is A Vintage Gibson LG-2 Worth?
faqs.a: The guide ranges are $6,000 to $8,000 for a spruce-top Banner LG-2, $5,000 to $7,000 for 1946 to 1949, and $2,700 to $5,350 for 1950 to 1962. They assume excellent original condition and the original case. Repairs and changed parts need separate appraisals.

faqs.q: Do Identical Rows Mean Every Year Sells For The Same Amount?
faqs.a: No. Adjacent years can share a broad model or era range. The exact year, bridge, repairs and case help place an individual guitar within or outside it.

faqs.q: Can An LG-1 Use The LG-2 Price Range?
faqs.a: No. Their similar outline and sunburst finish don't make them the same model. I establish the model before choosing a price reference. The separate identification guide explains the construction differences.

faqs.q: Does A Replaced Plastic Bridge Make An LG Worthless?
faqs.a: No. A well-fitted wood bridge can make an instrument useful to a player, but it changes the originality description. I assess the replacement, surrounding top and disclosed work together instead of applying an automatic percentage.

faqs.q: Does A Refret Change The Originality Category?
faqs.a: A quality refret preserves the all-original classification of an otherwise original guitar. It removes museum-quality status. A replaced bridge, altered bracing or repaired neck is a separate condition issue.
